item.text: {"text":"Recommended design: build category-specific transition counts C[a,b] only from adjacent training interactions, excluding padding. Smooth with P(b|a)=(C[a,b]+αp(b))/(Σj C[a,j]+α), where p is training-only item popularity with a small pseudocount. α is prior mass; larger values shrink sparse rows toward popularity. Treat its value as a validation-selected hyperparameter, not an established optimum. Combine SASRec logits with log-smoothed transition probabilities using fixed component normalization: estimate means/stds on a seeded sample of training prefixes and candidates, clamp stds above ε, and save them with each checkpoint. Never recompute normalization over evaluation candidates: that would make scores depend on the candidate set. This follows the training-only transformation principle in [scikit-learn’s guidance](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/common_pitfalls.html). Unseen source rows use p; empty histories should explicitly return the popularity fallback, bypassing potentially undefined all-padding neural features.\n\nUse one shared scorer, score(features, items, source_items), throughout prediction and diagnostics. For diagnostic position t, pass sequence[:,t], aligned with the causal feature predicting positive[:,t]; apply the nonpadding target mask. Deployment supplies the last nonpadding history item. Preserve predict_score(features, items) compatibility through an adapter, but pass source IDs explicitly from architecture-aware probes rather than guessing them from features or mutable cached state. Store counts in sorted CSR rows, enabling efficient row access as documented by [SciPy](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.sparse.csr_matrix.html). Candidate scoring gathers embeddings and sparse counts directly. Full-catalog scoring uses chunked matrix multiplication, initializes the analytic smoothed popularity contribution, and adds corrections at observed transition destinations; avoid dense item-by-item matrices. Serialize counts, popularity, smoothing, normalization, ensemble weights, routing and fallback rules through the predictor writer. These are implementation recommendations, not measured benchmark gains."}
